ad-1Qw8.title: Google car: Gen 3 with medium-short antenna
ad-1Qw8.summary: Only Gen 2 and Gen 3 exist. Gen 3 shows a medium-short antenna on the car and is by far the most common. Gen 2 is rare, mostly small side roads.

ad-3F4R.title: Landmark: Caldea tower and sky wheel
ad-3F4R.summary: In the capital you often see the tall Caldea spa tower and a sky wheel (Ferris wheel).

ad-4Dnj.title: Language: carrer means street
ad-4Dnj.summary: The Catalan word for street is carrer. Seeing it on a sign points to Catalan-speaking areas.

ad-JMBH.title: Bollard: orange reflector
ad-JMBH.summary: Bollard with an orange reflector, seen now and then on the main highways. Spain uses the same one.

ad-LHX7.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 8 stripes
ad-LHX7.summary: The pedestrian crossing sign has 8 stripes on the crosswalk. Spain is the only other European country with 8.

ad-NHCC.title: Pole: wooden snow poles, mixed colours
ad-NHCC.summary: Snow poles are made of wood and can be painted in many different colours.

ad-OMfo.title: Landscape: capital in a high mountain valley
ad-OMfo.summary: The capital is a city surrounded by tall mountains. At 1023 m it is the highest capital in Europe.

ad-PGfc.title: Google car: many Gen 2 snow trekkers
ad-PGfc.summary: Lots of older Gen 2 coverage taken on foot or by snow vehicle, especially at ski resorts. More than any other country for its size.

ad-QX0k.title: Coverage: autumn colours everywhere
ad-QX0k.summary: All Gen 3 coverage was taken in October, so many leafy trees are orange and yellow.

ad-TBFy.title: Road works: yellow and turquoise cones
ad-TBFy.summary: Traffic cones in yellow and turquoise-green are used across the whole country.

ad-ZYyW.title: Language: Catalan, with i instead of y
ad-ZYyW.summary: Catalan looks like Spanish, but it writes i where Spanish writes y ("and") and has more words ending in consonants. Also used in eastern Spain.

ad-kLb3.title: Sign: km markers with CG and CS numbers
ad-kLb3.summary: Kilometre markers show road numbers starting with CG or CS. Spain has similar marker designs, so check other clues too.

ad-oy4W.title: Houses: stone buildings
ad-oy4W.summary: Stone buildings are everywhere. The same style appears in the French and Spanish Pyrenees, so it narrows things down but is not conclusive.

ad-vpA3.title: Town: ski town with shops, no trees
ad-vpA3.summary: In the east, a touristy town packed with shops and hotels. At 2080 m, the surrounding mountains have no trees.

ad-yQEn.title: Guardrail: yellow reflectors
ad-yQEn.summary: Guardrails have yellow reflectors. In Europe only this country, Spain and Belgium use yellow, so it narrows things down.

ad-zsXQ.title: Plate: orange dot on the left
ad-zsXQ.summary: European plate with an orange dot on its left side. No other European country uses it, so it gives the country away.
